leads.candidate: Massive white fig (Ficus virens), Domain 'outliers' group near Central Avenue/northern fig plantation
leads.reason: Exceptional single-tree candidate confirmed by direct fetch of the primary source this pass ('Heritage Trees in the Domain, Royal Botanic Garden Sydney', Noel Ruting, LandArc, 30 Oct 2015 final draft, landarc.com.au PDF, extracted and read in full): 'a massive specimen Ficus virens var. virens (white fig), listed as an outlier in this avenue/northern group... likely to date from the 1850s-1870s. An aerial photo image taken in 1943 shows this particular tree with a 22 metres canopy spread. Over the past 72 years it has almost doubled its canopy diameter... (height: 20 metres; canopy spread: 36 metres; dbh: 2.50 metres)'. IMPORTANT: a WebSearch AI summary of the same document gave DIFFERENT figures (30m height, 25m canopy, 1.90m dbh) which turned out to belong to a DIFFERENT white fig entirely, the one 'found in the eastern row of Central Avenue' mentioned in the same paragraph for comparison; the summary conflated the two trees. This is a live example of the 'search summary is a lead, never a source' trap and is recorded here so a future pass does not repeat the error: always use the fetched PDF's own text (20m/36m/2.50m dbh for the outlier), never the search-tool summary. Still only ONE source found this pass (the LandArc report itself); a second source and a translatable tree-level coordinate (the report's own lawn/bed numbering, e.g. DL5, DL6, DL10a etc, could not be matched to this specific outlier from the text alone; would need the report's site plan figures, which did not extract from the PDF text) are both still needed before it can ship. girth_cm if used: pi*250cm diameter = ~785cm (buttressed fig mass, not a clean trunk measurement, must say so).

leads.candidate: Queensland Kauri Pine, Elizabeth Bay House garden area, Elizabeth Bay (mhnsw.au Florilegium)
leads.reason: Fetched directly this pass: mhnsw.au/stories/florilegium-plants/queensland-kauri-pine/ gives real detail beyond the earlier general mhnsw.au citation: 'a kauri (then named Dammara bidwillii) was among a consignment of rainforest trees, palms and conifers... dispatched from the Botanic Garden to George Macleay, Alexander Macleay's son, in 1873', making a documented-planting-date age estimate possible (c.1873, ~153 years). BUT the same source describes the tree as 'standing alongside a hoop pine... between 20th-century apartment blocks in Elizabeth Bay', which searches this pass (Ithaca Road / Billyard Avenue apartment redevelopment articles) suggest is private apartment-block grounds rather than the public Elizabeth Bay House museum garden itself. No evidence of public access or street visibility was found this pass. Per hard rule 10 ('when in doubt, leave it out'), this stays a lead rather than shipping; needs either confirmation that the tree stands on Elizabeth Bay House's own public museum grounds, or documented evidence it is visible from a public street/footpath, before it can verify. Only one source (mhnsw.au) found for the tree itself in any case.

leads.candidate: Hunters Hill Moreton Bay Fig Tree (Wikidata Q116026869, SHR ref 1800191, coords -33.8304, 151.13618)
leads.reason: RESOLVED this pass to a specific address: Wikidata's P361 ('part of') links this entity to 'Glenrosa' (Q116026842), a heritage-listed house at 12 Mark Street, Hunters Hill NSW 2110 (SHR ref 1800192 for the house itself). The NSW Heritage Management System pages (hms.heritage.nsw.gov.au) 403'd to both curl and a browser user agent, so the actual SHR citation text could not be read this pass. Moved from 'needs a second source' to blocked-adjacent: this reads as a private residential property (a house called Glenrosa on a suburban street, not a museum, park or place of worship), and no evidence was found this pass that the fig is visible from Mark Street or otherwise publicly accessible. Do not ship without either (a) confirmation the tree stands on public land / is genuinely street-visible, or (b) the site becoming a public institution. Left in leads rather than blocked because the SHR page itself was never actually read (403); a session with browser access could resolve this definitively either way.

leads.candidate: Bunya Pine (Araucaria bidwillii) and Port Jackson Fig group, the Domain, near Hospital Road (LandArc heritage report)
leads.reason: Found this pass while reading the Domain heritage PDF in full: 'two old rainforest specimens near Hospital Road - Podocarpus elatus (plum pine) and emergent Araucaria bidwillii (bunya pine)... likely to be early components of the 1850s-1870s planting scheme rather than later infill planting under Maiden. Both trees are identified in Jones 1903 plan and are assessed as having high individual significance.' Reads as a pair/group rather than one clean collectible point, and is single-sourced (the same LandArc report already used for the white fig outlier above); no lawn/bed number or coordinate extracted from the text. Not pursued further this pass for time; worth a second source and a location fix in a future pass, and a decision on whether the bunya pine alone (rather than the pair) is the collectible point.
